Subject: Re: Production impact - repeated latency spikes this week

Camila —

We saw multiple 5–10s tail-latency spikes across our nightly batch scoring jobs on 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-09. This caused several downstream workflows to timeout and one reporting job to fail outright. Our SRE team has attached logs and traces (see attachment).

This is material for us: SLA in our contract guarantees 99.9% p99 latency for the dedicated pool. The incidents pushed us below that for the week and our Ops lead is asking for a commercial remediation / credits. We need a clear remediation plan, timeline to avoid recurrence, and a concrete proposal for commercial make-good.

Can you escalate? We’re preparing to brief procurement this afternoon and the execs are watching.

Thanks,
Lena Park
Head of Product Ops
OrbitalHealth

Subject: Fwd: Production impact - repeated latency spikes this week

Camila / Sean — I’ve picked this up as P1. Initial quick notes from infra:
- Root cause appears to be a combination of a heterogeneous batch that expanded sequence lengths beyond typical distribution plus a GC spike on the serving nodes during KV cache eviction. Hybrid effect caused bad tail latency for a small % (~1.6%) of requests in a narrow time window.
- We have mitigations: temporarily pin model variant to non-quantized run state for the affected pool, increase KV cache size to reduce eviction frequency, and apply a GC tuning patch we already validated on staging.
- I’ll run a smoke deployment tonight (11/10) at 10pm PT and report back.

Commercial implications: we should calculate impacted token count and p99 breaches for the week; recommend a provisional commercial credit offer to reduce noise for the customer while RCA completes.

Vivek
Head of Inference
Redwood Inference

Team — quick internal plan before the exec sync at 4pm PT today with Orbitals: 

1) Technical remediation (short term, <24–48h):
  - Deploy GC tuning and KV cache increase tonight (Vivek).
  - Pin variant and guardrail request sampling to prevent oversized batches (Sean).
  - Add targeted tracing for seq-length tail buckets and alerting.

2) Commercial stance (provisional offer):
  - Offer a one-time service credit equal to 8% of November hosting charges for the impacted dedicated pool, conditional on a signed contract amendment that clarifies SLO measurement windows and introduces a mutual runbook for incident triage.
  - If RCA shows systemic product defect requiring code changes, escalate to product and consider a larger remediation (TBD).

3) Customer communication: 
  - Camila to present technical fixes + provisional credit and contract amendment template at 4pm PT.

Please reply with objections or alternative numbers — procurement will seek the most conservative number.

— Camila

Proposed immediate actions:
- We will deploy the GC tuning and cache increase tonight (11/11) and monitor for 72 hours.
- We’ll provide daily SLO sampling reports and the filtered traces you asked for.

Provisional commercial offer (to avoid disruption while RCA finishes):

Options they want on the table:
A) Apply a billing credit that covers the estimated impact ($24k) now; sign the amendment post-credit.
B) Apply the provisional 8% credit now, and if RCA shows higher impact, Redwood tops up to full estimated impact.

We prefer option B if you’re willing to commit to a post-RCA top up cap and a timeline for the RCA (5 business days). Otherwise procurement will push for A.

Please advise by end of day Monday so we can close procurement review.
